description: CitySim supports urban energy planning by simulating the energy demand and supply of districts of several hundred buildings. The EPFL CitySim Solver is a command-line integrated solver that reads building geometry and thermo-physical properties in a CitySim XML file and Meteonorm CLI climate files, models stochastic occupant presence and behaviour and common HVAC systems, accounts for radiation exchange in the urban environment for renewable supply, and writes TSV results. It was validated against field surveys and ESP-r and passed IEA BESTEST. kaemco, a 2013 spin-off of LESO-PB, builds CitySim Pro, a graphical interface on the open-source solver, reports more than 500 registered users, and offers training, maintenance and data services, with applications including building-integrated PV, heating and cooling, and urban heat island studies with the city of Fribourg. Coverage: generic. Access: free solver download; CitySim Pro from kaemco. Licence: open-source solver. Caveats: the XML input format needs preparation. Simulation uses: district demand, solar potential and heat mitigation scenarios. Related records: EPFL campus CitySim coupling data, Meteonorm and umi.
